reasoning: The core themes carrying the implementation argument are overwhelmingly descriptive: they state what governors will be given control over, what will be published, how budgets will be devolved, and how inspection will work, but almost none explain why these particular mechanisms were chosen over alternatives, what evidence informed the timetable (April 2017, end of 2018, etc.), or what the costed assumptions behind the £1.3 billion or £10-14 million figures are. The strongest evidence found is in 'Governor Empowerment and Prison Autonomy', the theme that carries most of the argument: 'Building on the devolution of powers that have already been rolled out in six reform prisons... We will learn from what the reform prisons are doing and apply this to the rest of the estate' -- this gestures at prior experience as grounds for the rollout method, but does not say what was learned, include any data, or cite a source. 'Leadership Development and Capability Building' similarly references 'lessons learned from our four executive governors' without detail. Other core themes -- Performance Monitoring, Inspection Framework, Financial Management, Policy Simplification, Workforce Planning, Evidence-Based Policy -- contain no evidence at all for the delivery method chosen, only commitments and descriptions. The strongest counter-example against raising the score is that even the best-evidenced theme never names a source, a dataset, or a finding, only an unspecified prior programme. To reach level 2, the document would need to name and cite what the six reform prisons or four executive governors actually demonstrated, and link that finding explicitly to the design of the April 2017 rollout, budget formula, or costings.
